hook: Bordeaux study path (no event): Merlot and Cabernet Franc on the limestone plateau of the Right Bank

station.name: St Emilion
station.period: sheet 1991-2020, but temperature and precipitation 1995-2020, sunshine 2006-2020 (footnote)

tmean_apr_oct_C.how: mean of Apr..Oct monthly Tm, St Emilion 1995-2020

claims.claim: 7,103 ha inside the appellation outline (delimited area, not vines)

claims.source: EU single document PDO-FR-A0988 (2018 amendment file), 2.6; atlas communes list

claims.claim: 35 km east of Bordeaux; Dordogne 5.5 km
Two appellations on the same area: Saint-Émilion max 65 hl/ha, Saint-Émilion Grand Cru max 55 hl/ha; Grand Cru is an appellation, not a rank
claims.source: INAO data in the atlas (max_yield_hl_ha); Open Wine Atlas Study, Right Bank lesson

claims.claim: a limestone plateau overlooking the Dordogne to the south, bounded by the Barbanne stream to the north
claims.value: un plateau calcaire dominant la Dordogne au sud et limité par le ruisseau de la Barbanne au nord

claims.claim: Soils mostly limestone and clay-limestone; Merlot on clay soils, Cabernet Franc on limestone or sand and gravel
claims.value: sont en majorité calcaires et argilo-calcaires

claims.claim: Côtes: steep clay-limestone slopes edging the plateau; sandier soils towards the Dordogne
claims.source: Open Wine Atlas Study, Right Bank lesson

claims.claim: Climate oceanic but more continental, east of the Gironde department
claims.value: climat océanique tempéré du Bordelais, mais plus continental

claims.claim: 6 red grapes allowed: Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cot (Malbec), Carmenère, Petit Verdot (secondary)

claims.value: Le cépage très largement majoritaire est le cépage merlot N.

claims.claim: Classification first 1955, revised about every ten years, only Saint-Émilion Grand Cru wines; ranks Premier Grand Cru Classé A, B, Grand Cru Classé
claims.source: Open Wine Atlas Study, Right Bank lesson

claims.claim: Cabernet Franc is called Bouchet locally
